text:
Everything about her enchanted, everything about her attracted:

her gaze, her gesture, her smile, her walk...

The wit of France flowed from her mouth.

She was “full of grace,” like the Hail Mary;

whoever saw her could never forget her!


Innocent as water, clear as day,

blond and snowy as peerless Margaret,

at the influence of her celestial soul the dawn appeared...

She was full of grace, like the Hail Mary;

whoever saw her could never forget her!


A certain sweet and gracious dignity clothed her

in I know not what distant and singular prestige.

More than many princesses, she seemed a princess:

she was full of grace, like the Hail Mary;

whoever saw her could never forget her!


I had the privilege of meeting her on my dolorous path;

through her my longing came to an end,

and my poetry found arcane cadences.

She was full of grace, like the Hail Mary;

whoever saw her could never forget her!


How, how I loved her! For ten years she was mine;

but flowers so beautiful can never last!

She was full of grace, like the Hail Mary,

and to the Fountain of Grace from which she came,

she returned... like a drop returning to the sea!

translation.title: Gratia Plena
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the Marian refrain and the poem’s final return of the beloved to the Fountain of Grace.
